grh_986c723b46a10ae262d8.title: The Legend
paragraphs: Hardware dealer Ned Austin becomes an unwilling Western celebrity after newspaper publicity transforms him into a legendary retired gunfighter. At first Ned resents the attention, though his business prospers and politicians begin imagining a public career for him. The legend becomes dangerous when three real gunmen arrive to kill Ned and claim the fame for themselves. Ned decides to face them rather than endanger the town, but his friend Billy cleverly points out that only one killer can receive credit and that three men shooting Ned together would only enlarge the legend. The gunmen turn on one another, Ned survives without becoming a killer, and he finally begins to enjoy the advantages of his heroic reputation.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on May 21, 1979. It is listed as episode 76 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Marvin Miller, [[person|parley-baer|Parley Baer]], Tommy Cook, Vivi Janis, and Elliott Lewis. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, John Vornholt as writer, and Lorne Greene as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_988a348a3866731d07f8.title: One Man Air Force
paragraphs: A dramatization of the wartime career of fighter pilot Don Gentile traces his fascination with flying from reckless youthful aviation in Ohio to combat service against Germany. Once war comes, the instincts that worried his family become disciplined skill in the air, where he earns a reputation as an exceptional fighter ace while remaining personally shy and self-effacing.
